name: Parthenon
description: The Doric temple on the Acropolis still defines the Athens skyline. Marble columns and scaffolding share the hilltop site.

name: Acropolis Museum
description: A modern museum at the foot of the Acropolis displays sculptures with the rock visible through glass floors.

name: White Tower
description: Thessaloniki’s waterfront tower marks the harbour promenade. Inside, exhibits cover the city’s layered past.

name: Palace of Knossos
description: Reconstructed Minoan ruins sprawl on a hill near Heraklion. Red columns and fresco copies hint at Bronze Age Crete.

name: Theatre of Epidaurus
description: A remarkably preserved ancient theatre known for its acoustics. Stone seats climb an open hillside.

name: Plaka
description: Athens’ old neighbourhood climbs toward the Acropolis in neoclassical streets and tavernas.

name: Oia
description: Whitewashed houses and blue domes cling to the caldera cliff. Sunsets draw crowds to the western terraces.

name: Navagio Beach
description: A shipwreck rests on white sand at the foot of limestone cliffs. Most visitors arrive by boat.

name: Meteora
description: Monasteries perch on sandstone pillars above the plain. Footpaths and roads link several active houses.

name: Medieval City of Rhodes
description: Fortified streets of the Knights’ town still hold inns, walls and harbourside towers.

name: Athens Central Market
description: Varvakios agora sells meat, fish and produce under covered halls. Nearby eateries serve simple market meals.

name: Monastiraki food streets
description: Souvlaki, loukoumades and cafés pack the lanes around Monastiraki Square beneath the Acropolis.

name: Modiano Market
description: A restored covered market in Thessaloniki hosts deli stalls and restaurants under arched roofs.

name: Ladadika
description: Former oil warehouses turned into a dining quarter with meze tavernas and evening tables outdoors.

name: Municipal Market of Chania
description: A cruciform market hall in Chania sells Cretan cheeses, herbs and fresh fish.

name: Corfu Easter
description: Corfu’s Orthodox Easter is known for pot-throwing from balconies and processions through the old town.
